name: Ruslan Rahimkulov
current_role: Private investor (family holdings in OTP Bank, MOL, real estate), Budapest
profile: Ruslan Rahimkulov (47, Russian citizen living in Budapest) and his older brother Timur inherited the fortune of their father Megdet in 2020. Megdet ran Gazprom's Hungarian office and a Gazprom-MOL JV, and built big stakes in MOL and OTP Bank. The brothers still hold large OTP and MOL stakes and have been setting up Hungarian companies in real estate, energy, construction and tourism.
interesting_fact: Their father Megdet Rahimkulov was the richest person in Hungary before he moved back to Russia in 2008.
notes: Very private, with no public profile or official contact channels. Hungarian press coverage is often critical (Russia ties, Sopron property deal), so approach carefully. Weak fit for the podcast apart from the energy-holdings angle (MOL).

name: Stephane Bonvin
current_role: Founder, CEO and director, Investis Holding SA (SIX: IREN), Zurich

Investis has since sold its real estate services segment to focus on owning property.

name: Claire Bombardier
current_role: Bombardier founding-family shareholder (no executive role found)
profile: Claire Bombardier (Beaudoin) is a daughter of snowmobile inventor Joseph-Armand Bombardier. She married Laurent Beaudoin in 1959, and he ran Bombardier for decades, turning it into a rail and aerospace group. Their son Pierre Beaudoin is chairman of Bombardier. Her wealth comes from the family's stakes in Bombardier and BRP; Hurun listed her in 2014-2015.
interesting_fact: She married Laurent Beaudoin in 1959 while he was studying accounting at the University of Sherbrooke. He joined her father's company as comptroller in 1963 and became president in 1966, after the founder's death.
notes: Very private: no public statements, roles or contacts found, and I couldn't confirm whether she is alive (born c. late 1930s). The family's public faces are Pierre Beaudoin (Bombardier chair) and the J. Armand Bombardier Foundation / Musée de l'ingéniosité in Valcourt. Reaching her would mean going through the family, which the rules rule out, so low priority.

name: Jennifer Steinbrenner Swindal
current_role: General Partner and Vice Chairperson, New York Yankees
profile: Daughter of George Steinbrenner and one of four siblings who each inherited about a quarter of his estate in 2010. She is a Yankees general partner and vice chairperson. The family also holds stakes in YES Network, NYCFC, Legends Hospitality and AC Milan. Based in Tampa, she focuses on philanthropy, including running the New York Yankees Tampa Foundation.
interesting_fact: George Steinbrenner died in 2010, during a one-year repeal of the federal estate tax. That saved his four children an estimated $600 million.
deep_cut_fact: She was a Morehead Scholar at the University of North Carolina, where she majored in business. Her first job with the team was in the Yankees Public Affairs Department in 1984-85.

public_contacts.value: https://www.mlb.com/yankees/team/contact (New York Yankees official contact page)

notes: Her public activity is Tampa philanthropy: NY Yankees Tampa Foundation, Gold Shield Foundation, Boys & Girls Club of Tampa Bay and St. Joseph's Children's Hospital Foundation boards. Go through Yankees media relations or the Tampa foundation. She rarely gives interviews. Avoid the topic of her divorce.

name: Nihat Ozdemir
current_role: Co-founder and director, Limak Holding (daughter Ebru Özdemir chairs the board); reported 2025 board chairman of ÇEİS (Turkish cement employers' association)
profile: Mechanical engineer, born 1950 in Diyarbakır, who co-founded Limak in 1976 with university friend Sezai Bacaksız. Limak builds and operates infrastructure: Istanbul Airport (consortium member), hydroelectric plants (a top-10 Turkish power producer), cement, tourism. Özdemir led the cement and energy side. He was Turkish Football Federation president 2019-2022, and Limak is now moving into data centres.
interesting_fact: Before going into business he spent four years on the engineering faculty at what is now Gazi University. For a short time he was assistant to Necmettin Erbakan, who later became prime minister.
deep_cut_fact: He moved to Ankara in 1967 to study mechanical engineering and earned a master's in industrial engineering from Ege University in 1975, a year before founding Limak. He was also Fenerbahçe's deputy president and press spokesman before heading the Turkish Football Federation.
notes: Strong podcast fit: hydro and energy assets plus a new data-centre push. Limak says it is evaluating sites in Türkiye and the Gulf (https://www.cnbce.com/teknoloji/limak-yonetim-kurulu-baskani-ebru-ozdemir-veri-merkezi-yatirimlari-icin-turkiye-ve-korfez-ulkelerini-degerlendiriyoruz-h23324). Daughter Ebru Özdemir, the chair, is the more media-facing family member. Best route is press@limak.com.

name: Fu Guangming
current_role: Chairman, Fujian Sunner Development Co. (SZSE: 002299), Guangze, Fujian
profile: Fu Guangming founded what became Sunner Group, China's largest white-feather broiler producer and a major chicken supplier to KFC and McDonald's in China. He started with a small hatchery in Guangze county, Fujian, in 1983. He still chairs listed Fujian Sunner Development, which now produces over 600 million broilers a year, and he shares the fortune with his wife and his daughter Fu Fenfang, a company director.
interesting_fact: Sunner grew from a single flock and about 10 staff into a vertically integrated poultry group that produces over 600 million white-feather broilers a year.
deep_cut_fact: In 1983, aged 30, he quit a secure job at the Guangze County People's Armed Forces Department and borrowed RMB 20,000 to open a chicken farm. He told Yicai the idea came from his childhood: with so many siblings, the family's chickens were saved for his mother after childbirth.

public_contacts.value: snljj@sunnercn.com (Board Secretary Liao Junjie, Fujian Sunner Development)

notes: Rarely talks to Western media, so expect to work in Chinese. Best route is the board secretary's office (IR). Daughter Fu Fenfang is involved in management. Podcast angle is limited apart from the entrepreneurship story.

name: Charles Cohen
current_role: President and CEO, Cohen Brothers Realty Corp.; Chairman, Cohen Media Group
profile: Charles S. Cohen (born 1952) bought out his father and uncle and grew the family's Cohen Brothers Realty into roughly 12M sq ft of Manhattan offices and design centres (750 Lexington, Pacific Design Center). A lifelong film buff, he founded Cohen Media Group in 2008, built a classic-film library of 800+ titles and bought Landmark Theatres in 2018. Since 2024 a Fortress loan default has led to foreclosure auctions, and Forbes now lists him as a former billionaire.
interesting_fact: He produced the Oscar-nominated 'Frozen River' (2008) and distributed Asghar Farhadi's Oscar-winning 'The Salesman'. In 1985 he wrote the movie quiz book 'Trivia Mania'.
deep_cut_fact: At 16 he made his first short film, which won an honourable mention at the Kodak Teenage Movie Awards. He went on to major in English at Tufts (1974) and graduate from Brooklyn Law School (1977).
notes: Ongoing financial and legal trouble: the Fortress $534M loan default, a 2024 foreclosure auction and a 2026 court deadline. Avoid the subject, and note his billionaire status is doubtful now. The best hook is film and cinema restoration. Contact through Cohen Media Group publicity; no verified published email found.

name: Réal Plourde
current_role: Co-founder and Corporate Director, Alimentation Couche-Tard (Circle K)
profile: Engineer (Université Laval, HEC Montréal MBA) who joined Couche-Tard in 1984. He helped build it from a Quebec convenience chain into the global Circle K operator with 17,000+ stores and about $73B in revenue, serving as COO and EVP and as chairman 2011-2014. He retired from management in 2011 and still sits on the board. One of four co-founders made billionaires by the company.
interesting_fact: Couche-Tard has made four of its co-founders billionaires: Alain Bouchard, Richard Fortin, Jacques D'Amours and Plourde.
deep_cut_fact: Before Couche-Tard he worked on engineering projects in Canada and Africa. In 2018 he and his wife Ariane Riou received the Lieutenant Governor's Seniors Medal for volunteer work, notably at the palliative care home in Laval.
notes: Low-profile Quebec engineer, so his engineering background and EV-charging/fuel-retail transition are natural podcast hooks (Circle K runs EV chargers). Route through Couche-Tard corporate communications.

name: Vincent Lo
current_role: Chairman, Shui On Group and Shui On Land (HK: 272)
profile: Vincent Lo Hong-sui (born 1948, Hong Kong) founded the Shui On construction and building-materials group and its property arm Shui On Land. Shui On Land is best known for turning a run-down Shanghai neighbourhood into the Xintiandi shopping and entertainment district. He has chaired the HK Airport Authority (2014-15) and the HK Trade Development Council (2015-19), and is handing day-to-day leadership to his daughter Stephanie, vice chairman of Shui On Land.
interesting_fact: He was an early mover into mainland China: he began investing in Shanghai in 1984, building a hotel there with the Communist Youth League, long before Xintiandi made Shui On famous.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating (reportedly from the University of New South Wales), he started his first business with HK$100,000 borrowed from his father, property tycoon Lo Ying-shek, rather than joining the family firm Great Eagle. He received Hong Kong's highest honour, the Grand Bauhinia Medal, in 2017.
notes: Prominent HK establishment figure. Avoid the family trust feud and the Trump lawsuit. The best route is Shui On Land corporate communications or IR; the contact page is JS-rendered, so I couldn't extract an email. Shui On has low-carbon and urban-regeneration angles.
